newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-H.Smith sees 96/97 capex at A$90 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-H.Smith sees 96/97 capex at A$90 mln.

text.p: Hardware, engineering and shipping group Howard Smith Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected to spend about A$90 million on capital expenditure (capex) in 1996/97.
"Our capex overall, we expect to be about A$90 million," managing director Ken Moss told reporters at a media briefing.

Moss said the company would concentrate the majority of its 1996/97 investment in its hardware division with another nine Hardwarehouse stores planned for New South Wales in the current year. In addition, the company was considering further stores in both Victoria and Queensland.
"By far the bulk of our investment will be in hardware," he said. "That's where we see the most lucrative opportunities and the ones that will most quickly be on stream."
He said the company would spend about A$180 million on the new Hardwarehouse stores in 1996/97, financed both through capital expenditure and lease back arrangements.
Moss also said the company had properties under review in both Western Australia and South Australia as possible Hardwarehouse sites.
Howard Smith currently operated 15 Hardwarehouses with another scheduled to open in Victoria in October, he said.
The company earlier reported an annual net profit of A$86.13 million, up from A$81.15 million previously.
Its shares ended 14 cents higher at A$8.75.
